name: maize
sowing_season: Kharif: June–July | Rabi: Oct–Nov | Spring: Feb–March
soil: Well-drained loamy soil, pH 6.0–7.5. Does not tolerate waterlogging.

stages.name: Germination / Emergence
stages.description: Seeds germinate and emerge within 5–7 days.
stages.irrigation: One pre-sowing irrigation. Light irrigation after sowing if soil is dry.
stages.fertilizer: Basal: 40 kg DAP + 20 kg MOP + 20 kg Urea per acre before sowing.
watch_for: Cutworm cutting seedlings at base at night

stages.name: Seedling (V3–V6)
stages.irrigation: Irrigate every 7–10 days. Critical to avoid water stress.
stages.fertilizer: Top dress 1: 30 kg Urea at 20–25 days after sowing.
watch_for: Fall Army Worm (FAW) — most destructive pest
Zinc deficiency (white stripe on young leaves)
tips: Check the whorl for FAW — apply sand+Chlorpyriphos mixture into whorl

stages.name: Vegetative (V7–V12)
stages.description: Rapid growth. Tassel initiation inside plant.
stages.irrigation: Irrigate every 7–8 days. This is a high water demand period.
stages.fertilizer: Top dress 2: 25 kg Urea at 45 days after sowing.
tips: Most critical period for FAW — weekly scouting essential
Apply Emamectin benzoate 0.4 g/litre into whorl for FAW

stages.name: Tasseling / Silking
stages.description: Tassel emerges at top. Silks appear on cob. Pollination occurs.
stages.irrigation: Most critical irrigation period — do NOT allow moisture stress during silking.
stages.fertilizer: No fertilizer. Avoid any spraying during pollination.
tips: Silk emergence and pollination window is only 7–10 days — protect carefully
Hot dry winds during silking cause poor grain set

stages.name: Grain Filling
stages.description: Cob and grains fill. Starch accumulates.
stages.irrigation: Irrigate every 8–10 days. Avoid water stress during grain filling.
tips: Ear rot is worse in humid conditions after silking
Monitor for ear rot — aflatoxin can build up in rotted grain

stages.name: Maturity / Harvest
stages.description: Husk dries. Black layer forms at grain tip. Grain moisture drops to 20–25%.
watch_for: Delayed harvest increases mould and aflatoxin risk
Grain moisture above 25% causes storage problems
tips: Dry grain to below 13% before storage to prevent aflatoxin

common_pests.name: Fall Army Worm (FAW)
common_pests.symptoms: Ragged feeding in whorl, frass (sawdust-like excrement), caterpillar with inverted Y on head
common_pests.control: Emamectin benzoate 0.4 g/litre into whorl; Spinetoram 0.5 ml/litre

common_pests.name: Stem Borer
common_pests.symptoms: Dead heart, shot holes in leaves, larva inside stem
common_pests.control: Chlorantraniliprole 0.3 ml/litre or Carbofuran granules in whorl

common_diseases.name: Downy Mildew
common_diseases.symptoms: White striping on young leaves, excessive tillering, stunted growth
common_diseases.control: Metalaxyl seed treatment; spray Metalaxyl 1 g/litre

common_diseases.name: Turcicum Blight (Northern Leaf Blight)
common_diseases.symptoms: Long elliptical tan lesions on leaves
